questions.prompt: Atropine produces its effects by

options.text: blocking nicotinic receptors at the neuromuscular junction

questions.explanation: Blocking muscarinic receptors causes dry mouth, dilated pupils and tachycardia. Inhibiting acetylcholinesterase, by contrast, raises acetylcholine and produces the opposite effects.

questions.prompt: Neostigmine is useful in myasthenia gravis because it

options.text: inhibits acetylcholinesterase, increasing acetylcholine at the neuromuscular junction

questions.explanation: More acetylcholine remains to stimulate the weakened receptors, improving muscle strength.

questions.prompt: Salbutamol relieves asthma by

options.text: blocking muscarinic receptors in the heart
stimulating beta-2 adrenergic receptors, causing bronchodilation

questions.explanation: Beta-2 stimulation relaxes bronchial smooth muscle. Tremor and tachycardia are common side effects. Blocking beta-1 receptors slows the heart rather than opening the airways, and leukotriene inhibition is the action of montelukast.

questions.prompt: Propranolol should be avoided in asthma because it

options.text: is a beta-2 agonist that overstimulates the bronchi
is a non-selective beta blocker that can cause bronchospasm

questions.explanation: Blocking beta-2 receptors in the airways can provoke an attack. A cardioselective agent is safer, but is still used with caution.

questions.prompt: The first-line drug for anaphylaxis is
questions.explanation: Adrenaline reverses bronchospasm, vasodilation and oedema quickly. Antihistamines and steroids are adjuncts, which are too slow to be the first treatment. Atropine has no role in reversing anaphylaxis.

questions.prompt: A dry persistent cough is a recognised side effect of

options.text: enalapril, an ACE inhibitor, due to accumulation of bradykinin
amlodipine, due to blockade of calcium channels
losartan, due to blockade of AT1 receptors
furosemide, due to loss of potassium

questions.explanation: ACE also breaks down bradykinin, so inhibiting it causes bradykinin to build up. Losartan does not do this, which is why it is used when cough occurs.

questions.prompt: A common adverse effect of amlodipine is
questions.explanation: Dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers dilate arterioles, so fluid leaks into the tissues of the legs. Cough is typical of ACE inhibitors.

questions.prompt: Losartan lowers blood pressure by
questions.explanation: ARBs act at the receptor, whereas ACE inhibitors prevent angiotensin II formation. Both are contraindicated in pregnancy.

questions.prompt: Furosemide acts by inhibiting the

options.text: Na-Cl co-transporter in the distal tubule
aldosterone receptor in the collecting duct
Na-K-2Cl co-transporter in the thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle
carbonic anhydrase in the proximal tubule

questions.explanation: This blocks reabsorption of a large share of filtered sodium, so it is a powerful diuretic. The distal tubule transporter is the target of thiazides.

questions.prompt: Spironolactone, an aldosterone antagonist, can cause
questions.explanation: By blocking sodium reabsorption in exchange for potassium, it retains potassium. Loop and thiazide diuretics, in contrast, tend to cause hypokalaemia.

questions.prompt: Thiazide diuretics such as hydrochlorothiazide act on the

options.text: distal convoluted tubule, inhibiting the Na-Cl co-transporter

questions.explanation: They are used for hypertension and may cause hypokalaemia and hyperuricaemia. Loop diuretics act on the thick ascending limb.

questions.prompt: Warfarin acts by

options.text: inhibiting vitamin K epoxide reductase, reducing synthesis of factors II, VII, IX and X

questions.explanation: It prevents recycling of vitamin K needed to activate the clotting factors, and its effect is monitored by the INR. Heparin works through antithrombin III.

questions.prompt: The antidote for heparin overdose is
questions.explanation: Protamine binds heparin and neutralises it. Vitamin K reverses warfarin and is slower, which is why it is the nearest wrong choice.

questions.prompt: Aspirin has an antiplatelet effect because it

options.text: irreversibly inhibits cyclooxygenase-1, reducing thromboxane A2

questions.explanation: Platelets cannot make new enzyme, so the inhibition lasts for the life of the platelet. Warfarin, not aspirin, acts on vitamin K.

questions.prompt: Naloxone is used to treat

options.text: opioid overdose with respiratory depression and pinpoint pupils

questions.explanation: Naloxone is a competitive opioid antagonist. Flumazenil is the antagonist for benzodiazepines. Paracetamol overdose is treated with acetylcysteine, and organophosphate poisoning with atropine and pralidoxime.

questions.prompt: Carbamazepine controls focal seizures mainly by

options.text: enhancing GABA release by blocking calcium channels

questions.explanation: It stabilises neuronal membranes by prolonging the inactive state of sodium channels, so repetitive firing is reduced. Blocking calcium channels is the action of ethosuximide, and carbonic anhydrase is the target of acetazolamide.

questions.prompt: Metformin lowers blood glucose mainly by

options.text: reducing hepatic gluconeogenesis and improving insulin sensitivity
stimulating insulin release from beta cells

questions.explanation: It does not stimulate insulin secretion, so on its own it seldom causes hypoglycaemia. Sulfonylureas, the nearest wrong choice, stimulate insulin release.

questions.prompt: Digoxin increases the force of cardiac contraction by

options.text: inhibiting the Na+/K+ ATPase pump, raising intracellular calcium

questions.explanation: Higher intracellular sodium reduces calcium removal, so contractions strengthen. Hypokalaemia increases the risk of digoxin toxicity. Blocking calcium channels, blocking beta-1 receptors and opening potassium channels are the actions of other drugs, and none of them raises intracellular calcium.

questions.prompt: Statins, such as simvastatin, lower cholesterol by inhibiting
questions.explanation: This blocks an early step in hepatic cholesterol synthesis. A well-known adverse effect is myopathy. Lipoprotein lipase is activated by fibrates, pancreatic lipase is inhibited by orlistat, and cyclooxygenase is inhibited by aspirin.

questions.prompt: Omeprazole reduces gastric acid by

options.text: irreversibly inhibiting the H+/K+ ATPase (proton pump) of parietal cells

questions.explanation: The proton pump is the final step of acid secretion. H2 blockers such as ranitidine are the nearest wrong choice, as they act earlier in the pathway.
